Why is a squared plus b squared equal to c squared?
Take a right triangle. Its short sides are a and b. The long side is c.
Place them inside a square of side a plus b.
The long sides form a tilted square in the middle. Its side is c.
So the big square is four triangles, plus c squared.
Now slide the triangles into two corners.
The same four triangles. But the space left over is now two squares, a squared and b squared.
The big square has not changed. The triangles have not changed.
So what is left must match. c squared equals a squared plus b squared.
